E1.evidence: Issue #976 gives a reproducer ("ros2 service call /rosapi/message_details rosapi_msgs/srv/MessageDetails \"{'type': 'sensor_msgs/JointState'}\"") and the full traceback ending in "[rosapi_node-5] KeyError: 'check_fields'" and "[ERROR] [rosapi_node-5]: process has died [pid 6530, exit code 1, ..." (https://github.com/RobotWebTools/rosbridge_suite/issues/976). The maintainer approved and merged PR #1031 and closed the issue with "Fixed by #1031".

E2.evidence: rosapi (rosbridge_suite) introspects generated Python message classes by walking __slots__ and looking each slot up in _fields_and_field_types (objectutils._handle_array_information / _handle_type_and_array_len at 2.1.0: "field_type = instance._fields_and_field_types[name[1:]]"). rosidl_generator_py (ros2/rosidl_python), which generates those classes, added a non-field slot '_check_fields' to every message's __slots__ in commit 6d5d5048 (#194, first released in 0.18.0 for Iron). The generated classes' declared attributes changed across the boundary between two separately released packages. The fix is in the consumer, but the failure depends on the consumer's assumption about the provider's generated API, so it is not internal. Steps 3-5 do not apply.

E3.evidence: UPGRADE: the provider runs at a Jazzy release (0.22.0) whose templates include '_check_fields', while rosapi's introspection code still assumes the pre-Iron generated-class layout: "There's a change in the Python message generator that landed in Iron (and newer distros) that appears to breaking the array handling in rosapi." (https://github.com/RobotWebTools/rosbridge_suite/pull/1031).

E4.evidence: Observed failure: rosapi_node crashes on the service call ("KeyError: 'check_fields'", "process has died") (https://github.com/RobotWebTools/rosbridge_suite/issues/976).

units.name: rosidl_generator_py
units.revision_basis: The reporter runs ROS 2 Jazzy binaries (paths /opt/ros/jazzy/...) and names only the distro for this package. rosdistro jazzy/distribution.yaml at the last commit before the report (43514a34, before 2024-11-20T18:17Z) lists rosidl_python release 0.22.0-2. Tag 0.22.0 (2155a8ec, 2024-04-16) has '_check_fields' in the __slots__ template (rosidl_generator_py/resource/_msg.py.em line 212). The sensor_msgs/std_msgs/builtin_interfaces Python classes in the binaries were generated by whichever Jazzy rosidl_generator_py release was current when they were built; every release from 0.18.0 on contains the slot. The resolution does not change the provider.

units.name: rosapi
units.revision_basis: Broken: the reporter states "Library Version: 2.1.0" (tag 2.1.0 = 0f3b1f5e, 2024-10-07); the traceback line numbers match objectutils.py at that tag (line 194 "field_type = instance._fields_and_field_types[name[1:]]"). Resolved: merge commit of PR #1031 on the ros2 branch (2025-05-18), first contained in tag 2.3.0.

failed_conditions.quote: Iron’s `rosidl_generator_py` templates now inject extra private slots (e.g. [_check_fields](https://github.com/ros2/rosidl_python/blob/iron/rosidl_generator_py/resource/_msg.py.em#L212)) into every message’s `__slots__`. Those names don’t appear in the message’s `_fields_and_field_types` dict, so code that blindly walks `__slots__` will hit a KeyError.

loudness_evidence: No existing tooling reports a mismatch at build, connection, or activation. The failure appears only as an unhandled exception in rosapi's own code when the service is called: "[rosapi_node-5] KeyError: 'check_fields'" and "[ERROR] [rosapi_node-5]: process has died [pid 6530, exit code 1, ..." (https://github.com/RobotWebTools/rosbridge_suite/issues/976).

resolution.summary: Consumer-side change: PR #1031 (merge 005747b7) changes rosapi objectutils._handle_array_information to skip any slot whose name (leading underscore stripped) is not a key of _fields_and_field_types, and adds a unit test with a mock message that has a '_check_fields' slot. The provider is not changed.
resolution.evidence: The patch author shows the patched rosapi answering the reproducer call ("This seems to fix the issue:" followed by a MessageDetails_Response listing fieldnames=['header', 'name', 'position', 'velocity', 'effort'], https://github.com/RobotWebTools/rosbridge_suite/issues/976#issuecomment-2880232385). The distro and the revisions of both units in that run are not stated, so the resolved composition is not identified by revision.

notes: Canonical forms: '__slots__' and '_fields_and_field_types' are class attributes that rosidl_generator_py generates into every message class. They are recorded as api:<attribute> because the consumer uses them generically, not for one type. The msg: elements are the types walked recursively in the reported call (JointState -> Header -> Time); their Python classes are code generated by the provider (shipped in sensor_msgs/std_msgs/builtin_interfaces). The class is element_retyped because the declaration of __slots__ changed (it gained a non-field entry) while the attribute is still present. definition_mismatch is not used because no .msg definition changed. consumer_built_against.broken is tag 0.17.0 (e6d72487), the parent of commit 6d5d5048 that added '_check_fields' (the last generator revision whose __slots__ held only field slots). It is inferred from rosapi's code, which assumes every slot maps to a field. The inferred span 0.17.0..0.22.0 also contains unrelated generator changes. The reporter first saw the problem through the rosbridge websocket server and reproduced it with the ros2 service CLI. The client-to-rosapi service composition (/rosapi/message_details) itself worked until the handler crashed, so it is not a separate condition. The same generator change also affects rosapi's service request/response typedef paths (get_service_request_typedef etc. use _get_typedef); the source shows no separate failure for them.
